label: Bible Study
prompt: But thou, O man of God, _____ these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness.
verse: But thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness.
note: Run from the love of money, run toward godliness — Paul's two-way race for Timothy.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Turn again, and tell Hezekiah the captain of my people, Thus saith the LORD, the God of David thy father, I have heard thy _____, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will heal thee: on the third day thou shalt go up unto the house of the LORD.
verse: Turn again, and tell Hezekiah the captain of my people, Thus saith the LORD, the God of David thy father, I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will heal thee: on the third day thou shalt go up unto the house of the LORD.
note: To sick King Hezekiah: I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears — and God added fifteen years.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And the LORD said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, that it may become _____ throughout all the land of Egypt.
verse: And the LORD said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
note: Modern versions often say gnats; the KJV says lice — the plague where Pharaoh's magicians finally admitted, 'This is the finger of God.'

label: Deep Water
prompt: What mean ye, that ye use this proverb concerning the land of Israel, saying, The fathers have eaten _____ grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge?
verse: What mean ye, that ye use this proverb concerning the land of Israel, saying, The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge?
note: The exiles' excuse proverb: our fathers sinned, we suffer — God answers that each soul answers for itself.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are _____, but not in despair;
verse: We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair;
note: Paul's paradox list: troubled but not distressed, 'perplexed' but not in despair.
